knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A proposal is based on visit records and evidence. Impressions and mood are not evidence.
A change starts only after written approval by the contract owner. A proposal does not change the contract.
A recurring item is raised as a written proposal with the evidence. It is not silently absorbed or stopped.

practicalCriteria: Identifies a mismatch from sample visit records over a defined period, separating one-off events from patterns.
Writes a change proposal with evidence, time and product implications, limits and options, and labels any example figure.
Refers a simulated item outside routine cleaning, and does not start or promise the change.
passRule: Mismatch identified from records, proposal written with evidence and implications, referral made for any item outside routine cleaning, and change not started or promised. Observed in a desk exercise. A knowledge check result is not a practical pass.
evidenceRequired: Evidence summary from sample visit records
Written proposal and the approval decision record
Referral record for any item outside routine cleaning
stopWorkCriteria: Changed work started before written approval
New price or frequency promised to the client
Growth needing investigation cleaned as routine without referral
